posts.author: MichaelH
posts.content_md:
How much light does your home made material block? If you put an unprocessed plate in front of your reference beam is there much difference between the pass-through and unobstructed light?

Have you tested your laser in an interferometer to determine what its coherence length is? It's possible, though not too likely, that your laser has a short CL.

posts.author: ErichRose
posts.content_md:
2 minutes with 20mws?! Are you shooting big plates? 4x5s? For a single beam set up that seems really long. 

Have, or can, you test the power output? I also agree that you should set up and tset the coherence length. Not all HeNes have good CD.

posts.author: MichaelH
posts.content_md: Even for 4x5 that's a long time. I'd also worry about stability over a 2 min exposure.

posts.author: Hans
posts.content_md:
40 seconds seems about right for homemade film. That's about what it takes with the film I made according Jeff Blyth's diffusion method. If the hologram looks foggy after exposure, it is usually an indication of over exposure.

What kind of developer do you use? If you use Ascorbic TJ-1 developer, the film should turn black in about 5 to 10 seconds for a good hologram.

posts.author: d paul
posts.content_md:
Hans

My standard developer is gp-2 diluted 15ml/200ml d.w. with a development time of 4 min. The film usually darkens in about a minute ,and then I soak in 70% and 99% IPA for 3 min each. After a minute in the 99%, the image begins to appear.

 I've tried Saxby's ascorbate developer with phenodine instead of metol, but only got one or two images out of a bunch of exposures. I have also tried cutting the exposure time in half ,and I get no image at all.

Rob

posts.author: Hans
posts.content_md: I have no experience with the Russian GP-2 developer. But I notice that you use double the concentration and one third the recommended development time. Did you do this to prevent fogging, or perhaps to increase fringe contrast?

posts.author: d paul
posts.content_md:
Hans,I did it that way to decrease the fogginess I was getting at the regular concentration/time. For Lippmann photos I use 15ml GP-2 to 100ml d.w. and 3 min developing time

rob
